answer.rationale: The incumbent has refused to reopen price this cycle, and finance has mandated an 18% cost cut. The assembly line is running at 94% with no buffer, so delivery risk is high and I cannot afford to disrupt the supply. The primary supply contract expires in 14 days and does not auto-renew, so inaction means losing the contract entirely (which is catastrophic at 94% capacity). The low-cost vendor memory (memory_c2) shows that switching to a low-cost vendor cut unit cost sharply, onboarding was quick, and invoicing stayed accurate. Given the incumbent won't move on price, switching to the previously validated low-cost vendor is the only path to meeting the 18% cost reduction mandate. I will execute this as a small guarded test to validate before full migration, which addresses delivery risk.
